name: Equal Subset Sum (ESS) and Pigeonhole Equal Subset Sum (PESS) algorithms
description: Two related problems. PESS (Papadimitriou 1994): given n positive integers with sum < 2^n - 1, pigeonhole guarantees two different subsets with equal sums; Jin-Wu (ICALP 2024) found one in O*(2^{0.4n}) via a structural characterization of instances with few solutions, and Jin-Williams-Zhang (ESA 2025) refined to O*(2^{n/3}); this is the one setting where pigeonhole collisions turn into a 2^{n/3} (below 2^{n/2}) algorithm. ESS is the decision version without the pigeonhole promise: MNPW (ESA 2019) beat 3^{n/2} with O*(1.7088^n) via representations; Randolph-Wegrzycki (STOC 2026) gave 1.7067^n; Yamano-Shibuya (arXiv 2607.09289, Jul 2026) gave 1.6994^n time / 1.5664^n space; Ye (arXiv 2608.08260, Sep 2026) gave one-sided Monte Carlo O*((5/3)^n). Note: the two 2026 arXiv items in the task outline are ESS (not PESS) papers.
authors_year_venue: Jin and Wu, A Faster Algorithm for Pigeonhole Equal Sums, ICALP 2024 (arXiv 2403.19117); Jin, Williams, Zhang, New Algorithms for Pigeonhole Equal Subset Sum, ESA 2025 (LIPIcs 351, art. 86); Mucha, Nederlof, Pawlewicz, Wegrzycki, ESA 2019 (arXiv 1905.02424); Randolph and Wegrzycki, STOC 2026 (arXiv 2511.10823); Yamano and Shibuya, arXiv 2607.09289 (Jul 2026); L. Ye, arXiv 2608.08260v2 (Sep 2026)
status_and_verification: Mixed. 2608.08260 (Ye) read in full from alphaXiv text (single-author preprint, v2; not peer reviewed). 2607.09289 (Yamano-Shibuya): abstract and intro only. Jin-Wu and Jin-Williams-Zhang: abstract-level only via fetch/search, proofs not read. MNPW and RW26 cited via the 2026 papers' introductions, not read directly. [uncertain]
key_theorem_or_bound: PESS: O*(2^{n/3}) time (JWZ25), previously O*(2^{0.4n}) (JW24), poly-space O*(2^{0.75n}) (JW24); classical MITM 2^{n/2}. ESS: MITM 3^{n/2} <= 1.7321^n; MNPW19 1.7088^n; RW26 1.7067^n; YS26 1.6994^n time, 1.5664^n space, poly-space 2.5430^n (from 2.6817^n); Ye: time O((5/3)^n poly(n) + n^2 m), space O((5/3)^n poly(n)+nm) for n integers of m<=2^n bits, error 2^{-Omega(n)}, never outputs a non-solution (Theorem 2.13). [uncertain]
regime_exponents: PESS: n/3 and 0.4n versus n/2. ESS: exponents 0.7369..n = log2(5/3) n (Central branch worst case p=1/5), Mitm branch 0.7244n, Collide branch 5/7=0.714n, so 5/3 is the max over zero-density p of three branches. No overlap with 0.311n / 0.661n; those thresholds are specific to the repo's D* analysis. Note: n/3 PESS means each pigeonhole collision (sums < 2^n) is exploited at density where 2^n sums with 2^n - 1 bound force many collisions.
proof_type_and_tools: Combinatorial/probabilistic. PESS: structural characterization of instances with few equal-sum pairs (Jin-Wu) plus pigeonhole. ESS: representation technique (Howgrave-Graham-Joux), random primes for modular filtering, minimum-support solution D* in {-1,0,1}^n, branch on zero-density p, method of types, totally unimodular rounding (Ye). [uncertain]
quantitative_loss: ESS algorithms have only poly(n) losses per branch (random prime filtering, types), but the final constant (5/3) is the max over branches; no BSG/PFR style loss. PESS structural step is believed exponential in the exponent (0.4 -> 1/3), details unverified. [uncertain]
worst_case_vs_average_case: Worst case, randomized (Monte Carlo, one-sided). Average case ESS: 3^{0.387n} (Chen-Jin-Randolph-Servedio SODA 2022).
coefficient_set: ESS reduces to finding D in {-1,0,1}^n with <D,x>=0, D nonzero, so the natural coefficient set is {-1,0,1} (equivalently disjoint subset pair); representation lists use {0,1,2} with labels enforcing difference in {-1,0,1}.
subset_size_regime: All subsets; the zero-density p = z/n of a minimum-support solution plays the role of the subset-size regime (support (1-p)n = Theta(n) in Central branch).
relevance_to_Nc: ESS asks for one equal-sum disjoint pair among all subsets, which is a solution of the same type counted by N_c; the pigeonhole regime (sum < 2^n) guarantees N_c >= 1 and JWZ show how an abundance of collisions yields n/3. In Ye's Lemma 2.5-2.6 the number of representations K=2^{kappa n} of a solution D is explicitly counted (free zero coordinates), which is the kind of exponent-level counting C1 needs.
relevance_to_Dstar: Minimum-support solutions D* in the ESS papers play the role of structure: distinctness of sums on free zero coordinates forces |support| minimality (Lemma 2.6 in Ye). A reduction of hard-instance D* to the zero-density p parameter could connect to the 0.311n threshold, but no statement exists in the sources.
applicability_gap: PESS requires sum < 2^n (a promise unavailable for general Subset Sum); ESS has no promise and its gains (1.6667^n vs 3^{n/2}) are measured against the 3^{n/2} MITM, not 2^{n/2}; targets (Subset Sum with fixed t) are not covered. Pigeonhole collisions are for ALL subsets, not Theta(n)-subsets; no doubling or poly-doubling hypothesis used.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: ESS hard instances: no solutions at all (e.g. sums all distinct, superincreasing/Sidon-like sets with m >= n bits give NO). Ye's algorithm explicit worst-case at zero-density p = 1/5. PESS has no such family since a solution always exists.
dependency_chain: MNPW19 -> RW26 -> YS26 / Ye26 (ESS); Jin-Wu24 -> JWZ25 (PESS); both use HGJ representation or pigeonhole + structure; combines with CJRS for subset balancing and Wagner/dissection-type collision finding in a branch-or-bin argument.
constructiveness: Fully constructive (the algorithms output the pair; one-sided error, verifiable).
lean_formalizable: Pigeonhole existence for PESS (sum < 2^n implies two equal subset sums) is a trivial counting lemma formalizable mathlib-free; the algorithmic bounds are not.
computational_check: No computational scale reported in the sources read (theory). At n<=40 the repo scripts could exhaustively check PESS instances (2^n subset sums) and measure collision counts versus 2^{n/3}-type predictions. [uncertain]
next_experiment: For PESS-regime instances (sum < 2^n), count exact collisions N_c at n<=40 for random vs structured inputs and compare with the density threshold that JWZ's structural dichotomy uses; document the transition near 2^{n/3}.
open_issues: Whether JWZ's n/3 can be improved or extends to ESS-with-target; Ye 2608.08260 is a single-author preprint (v2) with no independent verification; 2607.09289 and 2608.08260 appear to be ESS papers although the repo outline labels them under PESS; JWZ proofs not read here. [uncertain]
